name: DBX Mail
description: Local-first mail workbench: multiple IMAP accounts, cached conversations, a rich composer, offline outbox and attachments kept on disk.
releaseNotes: Local-first multi-account mail workbench that runs as a DBX plugin: IMAP sync, conversation view, rich composer, attachments written to a real folder on disk and an offline outbox. Filesystem work (saving attachments, .eml import/export, folder browsing, raw message cache) is done by the bundled Rust sidecar, so the plugin page itself has no file or network access. v0.1.3: long messages scroll again — the workbench grid left its implicit row height to the content, so a tall body pushed the reader pane past the window and the scroll container had nothing to scroll (clientHeight equalled scrollHeight); the conversation list got the same fix for hundreds of threads. Page-level styles that newsletters ship (body{height:100%;overflow:hidden} around a fixed 700px table) are no longer applied to the message container, so wide mails are no longer clipped horizontally. Non-primary folders now sync: opening a folder that was never synced (uid validity 0) triggers a one-time sync, and the empty state plus the header refresh button sync only the folder you are looking at. Two sidebar folders with the same role no longer share a name, and the unread count follows the open folder. v0.1.0–v0.1.2: IMAP folder names are encoded as modified UTF-7 (RFC 3501) and an RFC 2971 ID is sent when the server advertises it, which fixes 163/126 answering SELECT with 'Unsafe Login'; remote images are blocked by default and fetched through the local sidecar as data URLs on request; mail <style> blocks are extracted and scoped to the message container so they cannot restyle the app; Tailwind preflight resets inside message bodies are undone element by element; dark mode strips hard-coded colours.
